questions.question: How does green computing reduce paper and office cost?
questions.solution_html:
• Green computing reduces paper and office cost by promoting electronic
  • communication, digital documentation, and paperless workflows, thereby
  • minimizing printing and storage expenses.

questions.question: Define Green Supply Chain Management (GSCM)
questions.solution_html:
• Green Supply Chain Management (GSCM) is the integration of environmental
  • thinking into supply chain activities such as product design, material

questions.question: Define server consolidation.

questions.question: Expalin the major problems associated with excessive paper usage.
questions.solution_html:
• Major problems associated with excessive paper usage
  • Excessive paper usage leads to several environmental and operational problems. Large
  • quantities of paper production contribute to deforestation, which destroys natural
  • ecosystems. The manufacturing process consumes significant energy and water
  • resources, increasing environmental impact. Paper waste also increases the volume
  • of solid waste in landfills. Organizations incur high costs for printing, storage, and
  • document management. In addition, transportation and disposal of paper contribute to
  • carbon emissions, affecting environmental sustainability.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Discuss the features of a green data center.
questions.solution_html:
• Features of a Green Data Center
  • A green data center focuses on energy efficiency and reduced environmental
  • impact. It uses energy-efficient servers and processors to minimize power
  • consumption. Advanced cooling systems such as efficient airflow management reduce
  • energy used for temperature control. Server consolidation and virtualization reduce
  • the number of physical machines required. Green data centers often use renewable
  • energy sources like solar or wind power. They also implement power monitoring and
  • energy management systems to track and optimize energy usage.
questions.final_answer: energy management systems to track and optimize energy usage
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Apply the provisions of the Kyoto Protocol to explain how it addresses global warming.
questions.solution_html:
• Application of Kyoto Protocol provisions to address global warming
  • The Kyoto Protocol is an international agreement designed to reduce greenhouse
  • gas emissions responsible for global warming. It sets legally binding emission
  • reduction targets for developed countries. The protocol introduces mechanisms
  • such as carbon trading, allowing countries to buy or sell emission allowances. It also
  • includes the Clean Development Mechanism (CDM), enabling developed countries to
  • invest in emission reduction projects in developing countries. These measures
  • encourage the adoption of clean technologies and renewable energy, helping reduce
  • global warming.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Describe the importance of employee and stakeholder engagement in implementing environmental practices.
questions.solution_html:
• Importance of employee and stakeholder engagement in environmental
  • practices
  • Employee and stakeholder engagement is essential for the success of environmental
  • initiatives. Employees help implement green practices such as energy conservation
  • and waste reduction in daily operations. Stakeholder involvement ensures support
  • from management, suppliers, and customers for sustainability initiatives.
  • Engagement increases environmental awareness and responsibility within the
  • organization. It also improves corporate reputation and transparency, encouraging
  • organizations to maintain environmentally responsible operations.
questions.final_answer: organizations to maintain environmentally responsible operations
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain the major phases in a Green Information System development and deployment.
questions.solution_html:
• Major phases in Green Information System development and deployment
  • Green Information System development involves several phases. The first phase is
  • requirement analysis, where environmental objectives and sustainability goals are
  • identified. The second phase is system design, focusing on energy-efficient
  • architecture and environmentally friendly technologies. The next phase is system
  • development, where software and hardware solutions are implemented. This is
  • followed by testing and evaluation to measure environmental performance. Finally, the
  • system is deployed and monitored, ensuring continuous improvement and efficient
  • resource usage.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Differentiate between RoHS and EPEAT with respect to their focus and scope in green computing.
questions.solution_html:
• Difference between RoHS and EPEAT
  • RoHS (Restriction of Hazardous Substances) is a regulatory directive that restricts
  • the use of toxic substances such as lead, mercury, and cadmium in electronic
  • equipment manufacturing. Its primary focus is on reducing hazardous materials in
  • electronic products.
  • EPEAT (Electronic Product Environmental Assessment Tool) is an environmental
  • rating system that evaluates electronic products based on several environmental
  • criteria such as energy efficiency, recyclability, and environmental design. While
  • RoHS mainly addresses hazardous materials, EPEAT provides a broader assessment
  • of overall environmental performance of electronic products.
questions.final_answer: of overall environmental performance of electronic products
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Discuss the concept and classification of carbon footprint related to IT infrastructure.
questions.solution_html:
• Concept and classification of carbon footprint related to IT infrastructure
  • A carbon footprint refers to the total amount of greenhouse gas emissions
  • generated directly or indirectly by activities related to IT infrastructure. These
  • emissions occur through the operation of computers, servers, and data centers.
  • Carbon footprints can be classified into direct emissions, produced by on-site energy
  • use and equipment operation; indirect emissions, generated from electricity consumed
  • by IT systems; and supply chain emissions, which arise from manufacturing
  • transportation, and disposal of IT equipment.
questions.final_answer: transportation, and disposal of IT equipment
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: How to change a conventional PC into a Green PC using suitable Green Computing practices.
questions.solution_html:
• Converting a conventional PC into a Green PC
  • A conventional PC can be transformed into a Green PC by adopting several green
  • computing practices. Power management features should be enabled to reduce energy
  • consumption when the system is idle. Energy-efficient hardware components such as
  • Energy Star certified devices can be used. Replacing CRT monitors with LCD or
  • LED displays significantly reduces power consumption. Unnecessary background
  • processes should be minimized to optimize system performance and energy usage.
  • Proper recycling and reuse of electronic components also contributes to
  • environmentally sustainable computing practices.
